title: Same prompt, three Claude 5.5 configs: Haiku XHigh vs Sonnet High vs Opus Low building a Three.js Minotaur
author: joaocamu
selftext:
I ran the exact same prompt through three model/effort configs, **Haiku XHigh, Sonnet High and Opus Low (all 5.5),** inside **DeepSeek Harness**, and stitched the three results into one video so you can watch them run side by side (labels are burned into each panel).

**The numbers from my runs**

|Config|Cost|Wall-clock|Tokens|
|:-|:-|:-|:-|
|Haiku XHigh|$1.20|35 min|10M|
|Sonnet High|$3.80|55 min|9M|
|Opus Low|$1.50|7 min|133K|

  
Cache hit was close to **96%** on all three runs, so most of those token totals are cache reads. Opus Low is the odd one out: a tiny fraction of the tokens and a fraction of the wall-clock, still producing a working app.

  
The task was a dark-fantasy benchmark: a realistic, fully interactive 3D creature built in **Three.js / WebGL**, with the whole thing written in code (no external assets, no downloaded `.gltf`/`.obj` model, no textures, all geometry procedural). Everything came from a context free session and a did not use a image for reference.

The prompt is deliberately over-specified so a human can judge the output at a glance:

* **One object only** — a gaunt, hunched, bipedal bull-headed beast of the deep mine shafts, standing alone in a minimal dark studio/showroom so it's the only thing on screen. No extra creatures, no scenery.
* **Silhouette and anatomy**: hunchbacked stance with slightly bent knees, shoulder hump about twice human height, broad chest tapering to a narrow ribcage, heavy bovine skull set low between massive shoulder blades, long asymmetric cracked horns, small deep-set blind eyes, long arms hanging past knee level, digitigrade legs with worn cloven hooves, and a tail that is actually a length of old steel winding cable fused into the flesh, fraying into loose wires at the tip. Plus a forged iron collar with brass rivets and a broken chain link.
* **PBR materials**: slate-black damp-stone skin (`#1E2530`) with patchy spine fur and visible bone ridges, desaturated aged ivory horns and hooves, rust / dried-blood stains (`#5A3F2B`), dull brass rivets (`#A88A4A`), aged pitted iron for the collar and cable, and dead matte eyes with no specular.
* **Interactions that actually have to work**: 360° orbit and close zoom, jaw/snarl, head tracking the camera, arm swing and hand flex, cable-tail sway, plus toggles for wireframe, anatomical/bones layer, studio vs. dark-cavern rim lighting, a turntable mode, and a reset. No fake buttons, no placeholders, no pre-rendered video.
* **Presentation**: physically based rendering, ambient occlusion, contact shadows, reflections, rim light on the silhouette, minimal dark background.
* Deliverable: a complete runnable browser app with local run instructions.



(this, of course, is an anecdote, not a controlled benchmark. Token counts are totals as reported by the harness; prompt caching does a lot of the heavy lifting on cost. api cost as reported by platform claude)

Which one do you think actually nailed the silhouette? Full prompt in the first comment.
